title: Stablecoin payment = FX operation (purpose code + client ID)
message: Brazil treats cross-border stablecoin payments as FX operations (Res. BCB 521, in force since 2 Feb 2026). Since 4 May 2026 the Brazilian VASP must collect from its client the BCB purpose code (Annex III up to US$50k per payment, Annex IV above) and details of the payer abroad. The client's CNPJ/CPF is needed for identification under Circular 3.978.

title: USD 100k cap per international stablecoin payment (non-bank VASP)
message: A non-bank Brazilian VASP (SPSAV) may not settle an international payment or transfer with virtual assets above the equivalent of US$100,000 when the counterparty is not an institution authorized to operate in Brazil's FX market (Res. 277 art. 29, IV). Route through a bank or the wire.

title: eFX providers can't settle with foreign counterparties in virtual assets
message: Since Oct 1, 2026, an eFX provider may settle with its counterparty abroad only via an FX contract or a non-resident BRL account; use of virtual assets (incl. stablecoins) is prohibited (Res. BCB 277, art. 50, I, as amended by Res. BCB 561/2026). Route via an authorized or in-transition VASP (Res. BCB 521) or a bank.

source.name: Res. BCB 561/2026, art. 1 (new art. 50, I of Res. BCB 277) and art. 4

title: Off-ramp's BCB authorization request is pending
message: Off-ramp is not yet BCB-authorized. It filed for authorization on time (deadline Oct 30, 2026) and may keep operating while BCB decides (Res. BCB 520 art. 88 §6). BCB can take up to 1,080 days (Res. BCB 548/2026). For cross-border payouts, its request must also cover the FX market (Res. BCB 277 art. 29 §5, added by Res. 521).

source.name: BCB Res. 520/2025 art. 88 I and §6; IN BCB 704/2026 art. 9; Res. BCB 548/2026

title: Off-ramp has not filed for BCB authorization
message: Off-ramp has not yet filed for BCB authorization. Providers already operating must file by Oct 30, 2026 or stop within 30 days (Res. BCB 520 art. 88 I and §7; IN BCB 704 art. 9).

source.name: BCB Res. 520/2025 art. 88; IN BCB 704/2026 art. 9

title: Missed the Oct 30 BCB filing deadline
message: Off-ramp did not file for BCB authorization by Oct 30, 2026. It must stop virtual-asset services by Nov 29, 2026 (Res. BCB 520 art. 88 §7), and from Nov 6 Brazilian banks and payment institutions may not deal with it (art. 91, as amended by Res. BCB 589/2026). Corredor policy blocks it from Oct 31. Use an authorized VASP or a bank.

source.name: BCB Res. 520/2025 art. 88 §7; art. 91 as amended by Res. BCB 589/2026

title: Banks may not deal with non-authorized VASPs (from Nov 6)
message: From Nov 6, 2026, Brazilian banks and payment institutions may not deal with VASPs that are 'not authorized' (Res. BCB 520 art. 91, as amended by Res. BCB 589/2026). The amended text no longer exempts pending applicants, but BCB's Sep 23 press note still does. Confirm the off-ramp's Pix/BRL banking partner before paying.

title: Banks can't offer crypto services to clients
message: Banxico Circular 4/2019 (rule 3.a): Mexican banks and fintech institutions (ITFs) may use virtual assets only for Banxico-authorized internal operations and may not provide clients exchange, transfer or custody of virtual assets. Use a non-bank virtual-asset platform registered with SAT as an Actividad Vulnerable (LFPIORPI Art. 17-XVI) that pays out over SPEI.

title: Off-ramp must be a CNV-registered PSAV
message: This off-ramp is not in the CNV PSAV registry. Unregistered providers must not exchange or transfer crypto for others in Argentina (CNV Normas Tit. XIV Cap. III art. 3, as replaced by RG 1172/2026; sanctions under Ley 27.739 art. 37). Argentine banks and payment apps may not offer or facilitate crypto (BCRA Com. A 7506 / A 7759), so USDT-to-ARS must go through a registered PSAV.

source.name: CNV RG 1172/2026, Boletin Oficial 15-10-2026 (Normas CNV Tit. XIV Cap. III arts. 1, 3, 4)

title: USDT/ARS rate vs. BCRA official rate
message: Business risk, not a legal rule: the USDT/ARS (crypto dollar) rate is more than 5% above the BCRA official wholesale rate. If the invoice is in pesos, agree with the supplier which rate converts it before paying.

source.name: BCRA Com. A 3500 wholesale rate (official API); USDT/ARS market rate (demo snapshot 2026-10-16)

title: Venezuela OFAC sanctions review hold
message: Policy hold pending sanctions review. This is a company control, not a country-wide legal ban: Venezuela is under targeted OFAC sanctions (31 CFR 591), and OFAC says U.S. persons may deal with the country and people of Venezuela when no blocked person is involved (FAQ 680). Blocked: the Government of Venezuela, including PdVSA, the central bank, state-owned companies and banks, and anyone acting for it (EO 13884); SDNs; and entities 50% or more owned by blocked persons (31 CFR 591.406). Before release, compliance must confirm that the payee, its owners and the receiving bank or off-ramp are not blocked, or are covered by a general license (e.g. GL 57 for named state banks).

source.name: OFAC Venezuela-Related Sanctions (31 CFR 591; EO 13884; FAQ 680)
